I.
REGULAR BUSINESS.  This section is for a wide variety of matters generally worthy of separate discussion such as the consideration of ordinances for introduction, resolutions, extraordinary policy and business matters, staff reports and recommendations. The presiding officer will take public comment on each Regular Business item.  Each speaker shall have up to three minutes for each agendized Regular Business item, as may be shortened or extended, or a cumulative limit on the time for all public speakers may be imposed, at the discretion of the Presiding Officer. Pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(b)(3), any member of the public wishing to address the legislative body directly pursuant to California Government Code section 54954.3 may do so at each teleconference location at the time the item is considered.
 
18.
CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION RATIFYING EMERGENCY WORK RELATED TO THE SKYLINE SLOPE FAILURE AND A RESOLUTION DELEGATING AUTHORITY TO CITY MANAGER, OR CITY MANAGER’S DESIGNEE, TO TAKE CERTAIN ACTIONS IN RESPONSE TO FUTURE EMERGENCIES UNDER THE PUBLIC CONTRACT CODE (4/5TH VOTE NEEDED)
Recommendations:
  1. Adopt the Resolution titled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LAGUNA BEACH, CALIFORNIA RATIFYING EMERGENCY TEMPORARY WINTERIZATION EFFORTS REGARDING THE SKYLINE SLOPE FAILURE NEAR 1525 SKYLINE DRIVE, 1535 SKYLINE DRIVE, AND 1587 ATLANTIC WAY AND FINDING THE PROJECT EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT”;
  2. Adopt the Resolution titled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LAGUNA BEACH, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING CITY COUNCIL POLICY NO. 4.4: CITY MANAGER AUTHORITY TO TAKE CERTAIN ACTIONS PURSUANT TO PUBLIC CONTRACT CODE SECTION 22050 TO BE ADDED TO THE CITY COUNCIL POLICY AND PROCEDURES MANUAL, AND FINDING SUCH ACTION EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT”; and
  3. Find that the recommended actions are exempt from the requirements of CEQA pursuant to Public CEQA section 21080 (b)(4), and CEQA Regulations section 15269 (c), as specific actions necessary to prevent or mitigate an emergency. Further, the proposed resolution adopting City Council Policy No. 4.4 is not a “project” under CEQA and has no potential to result in a direct or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change to the environment pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15378.
